_comment: The fifth source of truth, and the second half of grounding (see _index.md and the world_state.json sibling): objective rules of the current embodiment - true regardless of whether any character knows them, distinct from _lore/facts/ (true of being a person in this world at all, embodiment-independent). Every entry is tagged `embodiment` so a future different embodiment backend only has to swap the entries carrying that tag, never the mechanism. `distribution` decides access: `universal` entries are known by every character unconditionally, same shape as _lore/facts/ but embodiment-scoped rather than personhood-scoped; `contextual` entries are known only if the character's own routine contexts (see _lore/contexts.json's `grounding_provides`) provide a matching tag - computed live by scripts/lore/sample_grounding.py, never cached into a character file. Never folded into encodings.json and never sampled by sample_lore_knowledge.py, same isolation as facts.json - but unlike facts, grounding CAN be attributed (a character knows it because they've seen/used it themselves, first-hand) and CAN grow, hand-curated over time the same way _lore/tales/ does. This file is game-agnostic: populate it with the rules of your specific embodiment/world. See specific seed files (e.g. _test/*/grounding_mechanics.json) for populated examples. An entry's content can be either propositional/rule content (a fact about danger, survival, or how something works) or vocabulary/naming content (naming a concrete thing that exists in this world - e.g. 'cobblestone' - so a character can refer to a real material instead of a generic placeholder), or both; this is documentation only, not a new field or `type` distinction - see TODO.md's grounding-mechanics entry for the causal/recipe extension planned on top of this.
